title: MAMBench Phase 3 Memory Record
description: Canonical memory record schema for the Phase 3 clean agent. Narrative semantics are defined in memory_schema.md; this file is authoritative for field names, types, and required-ness. This schema defines STRUCTURE only -- it does not freeze creation thresholds, equivalence thresholds, or retrieval/selection algorithms, which remain experimental decisions for later Phase 3 stages.

memory_id.description: Globally unique, immutable identity. Never reassigned or reused, including after supersession or retirement.

memory_type.description: foundation = originates from the frozen Phase 2 UMR substrate (or a future legitimate-observation creation policy). derived = produced from one or more existing memories via an explicit, logged creation event.

content.description: The memory's content payload. Structure inherited from the Phase 2 Unified Memory Record for foundation memories; derived memories carry a content payload produced by the (not-yet-frozen) derivation mechanism.

source.description: Provenance pointer. For foundation memories: pointer to the originating Phase 2 UMR record (dataset, record id, hash). For derived memories: pointer to the derivation event that produced this memory.

reference_id.description: Identifier of the referenced UMR record or derivation event.

parent_ids.description: Direct parent memory_ids. MUST be empty for memory_type=foundation. MUST be non-empty for memory_type=derived. Multiple parents are explicitly supported (A,B -> C). Ancestry/descendant sets are computed by transitively walking these edges at query time -- never precomputed into a merged 'family' set.

creation_event.description: Identifier of the logged event (see relationship_schema.md event log) that created this memory.

creation_timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of memory creation.

lifecycle_state.description: Canonical lifecycle state. Reuse (retrieval, selection, usage) is modeled as an event, not a state transition. Retired memories are never deleted.

equivalent_to.description: Optional list of memory_ids this memory is materially equivalent to. Equivalence is a relationship between distinct identities -- it never causes identity merging.

conflicts_with.description: Optional list of memory_ids this memory conflicts with. Conflicting memories are both preserved; neither is silently overwritten.

superseded_by.description: If set, the memory_id of the memory that legitimately supersedes this one. This memory transitions lifecycle_state to RETIRED but is never deleted.
